_comment: What it takes to make an S3 bucket serve public avatars. Counted as infra.
This policy is only half of it. The other half is not a file and therefore
is not counted here, which flatters S3 in the LOC table:
1. Turn OFF BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy and
RestrictPublicBuckets, at BOTH the account and the bucket level.
2. Acknowledge the console warning that the bucket will be public.
3. Optionally front it with CloudFront + OAC, at which point you write an
origin access policy instead of this one and the bucket goes private
Step 1 is the one that produced the Fiverr/Cloudinary class of incident. It
is a decision with two options, one of which discloses data, and it produces
no error, no failing test and no observable difference in normal operation.
